title: The Sweet Summer
premise: Tamsin Joubert has spent seven years on the Cornish coast rebuilding after a fire that took her family's lighthouse cottage and her confidence, writing quiet novels and answering a decade of anonymous letters from 'W.' When the letters' author — Callum Wren, the boy she loved and blamed for everything — moves in next door to restore the decommissioned light station, she must confront the truth that she set the fire herself in a moment of panicked grief. As summer deepens, their collaboration restoring the lighthouse forces forgiveness of the person in the mirror, but Callum's visa is expiring and the council plans to demolish the tower. Tamsin must choose between her safe small life and fighting publicly for the light — and for him — ending with the relit lamp, a granted heritage order, and Callum staying as its keeper.
about_author: Rafael Kavanagh is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent five years cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction full-time. The Sweet Summer is his fourth novel and the first written from his grandmother's kitchen table overlooking a working light.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Establishes her careful life: morning swims, part-time bookshop shifts, a finished-but-unsubmitted novel, and the ritual of rereading one letter from 'W.' Emotional beat: contentment that feels suspiciously like hiding.

chapters.title: A Van at the Boundary Stone
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A removal van arrives at the derelict keeper's cottage next door; she watches a tall man unload boxes labeled with her childhood street address. Beat: unease sharpening into recognition she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Callum Wren
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Face-to-face at the garden wall; seven years collapse. He says he's leased the cottage to restore the old light station. She retreats inside and rereads every letter in one sitting. Beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: What the Letters Never Said
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. His arrival, his decade of unsigned letters, and why he came back: the council's demolition notice for the tower. He doesn't know about the fire's true cause. Beat: hope braided with guilt.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Argument
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin accuses him of cruelty disguised as devotion; he asks what he did that was so unforgivable. Neither tells the whole truth. Beat: anger as armor.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ashes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Flashback chapter: the night of the fire, her grandfather's death, and the lie she told everyone including herself. First time the reader sees she started it. Beat: buried grief surfacing.

chapters.title: The Council Letter
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He shows Tamsin the demolition notice and asks for her help — her grandfather's logs could win heritage protection. She refuses. Beat: duty versus fear.

chapters.title: Low Tide, Long Walk
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A forced encounter on the causeway strand; they walk and argue and almost laugh. He mentions the letters kept him sane abroad. Beat: the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Logbooks
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She opens the sealed box of logbooks she hasn't touched in seven years and finds her grandfather's final entry mentions 'the girl who will keep it lit.' Beat: being seen by the dead.

chapters.title: Terms of Truce
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They negotiate: she'll help archive the logs for the heritage bid, nothing more. A handshake that lasts too long. Beat: reluctant partnership.

chapters.title: Rain on the Archive Table
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Working side by side in the cottage; storm traps them overnight. He falls asleep mid-sentence; she reads his unfinished letter draft addressed to her. Beat: tenderness she can't afford.

chapters.title: The Village Remembers
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Gossip spreads; an old neighbor tells Callum the official story of the fire and watches his face carefully. Beat: dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: Submission Day
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They file the heritage application together; small celebration, wine on the cliff path, almost-kiss interrupted by her panic attack. Beat: desire colliding with trauma.

chapters.title: The Editor's Email
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Her agent wants her new novel — which is transparently about the fire and 'W.' Submitting means exposure. Beat: art demanding honesty.

chapters.title: Scaffolding and Confessions
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. On the tower scaffolding, Callum admits he left after the fire because Tamsin stopped answering him; the letters were penance for abandoning her. Beat: guilt met with silence.

chapters.title: Midsummer Fair
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The village fair; dancing, lanterns, a genuine happy day. Mrs. Penhale nearly reveals the fire's true cause to Callum. Beat: joy shadowed by approaching truth.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Wrote
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He finds her published short story in the bookshop and reads the narrator's confession of setting a fire. He misunderstands it as fiction. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Inspection
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Heritage officer visits; Tamsin speaks publicly about the lighthouse for the first time and discovers her voice. Beat: growing courage.

chapters.title: Visa Expiry
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. His restoration contract and visa end September 30th; if the heritage decision comes later, he'll be gone. He hides this from Tamsin. Beat: ticking clock installed.

chapters.title: Night Swim
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Moonlit swim; they finally kiss. Tamsin pulls back saying there's something he has to know first — then can't say it. Beat: intimacy and the secret pressing closer.

chapters.title: Mrs. Penhale's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The old neighbor gently tells Tamsin that carrying the lie alone is heavier than any truth. Tamsin drafts a confession letter and burns it. Beat: the mirror moment begins.

chapters.title: The Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. A gale cracks the tower's lantern room; emergency repairs needed or the demolition case strengthens. Community rallies; Tamsin works beside him all night. Beat: unity forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Found Photographs
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the logbook box, photos of young Callum and Tamsin on the gallery — and her grandfather's note pairing their names. Beat: permission from the past.

chapters.title: Almost Honest
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Callum starts to tell her about the visa; Tamsin starts to tell him about the fire; each deflects the other. Both go home sick with it. Beat: tragic near-miss.

chapters.title: The Hearing Date
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Heritage hearing scheduled October 14th — two weeks after he must leave. He applies for an extension and is refused. Beat: despair hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Chapter One of the Novel
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She rewrites her novel's opening to tell the truth outright and sends it to her agent. Beat: choosing exposure over safety.

chapters.title: The Gala Invitation
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A fundraiser for the restoration; she's asked to speak as the keeper's granddaughter. Public speaking terrifies her more than the fire. Beat: stakes made personal and public.

chapters.title: Gala Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin speaks shakily, beautifully; Callum realizes he loves her. They leave early, walk to the tower, and she begins: 'The fire was me.' Beat: the confession begins.

chapters.title: The Whole Truth
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Full flashback interwoven with present: grief over her grandfather's terminal diagnosis, the candle, the panic, the lie. Callum listens without flinching. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He processes: his letters went to the person who most needed them and least believed she deserved them. He tells her the visa news. Beat: honesty begetting honesty, then heartbreak.

chapters.title: Silence Between Cottages
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Two days of not speaking; she drafts the letter she should have sent ten years ago and slips it under his door. Beat: rock bottom turning.

chapters.title: The Reply
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He answers with the eleventh letter — signed, dated tomorrow, asking her to fight beside him even if he leaves. Beat: love stated without conditions.

chapters.title: Campaign for the Light
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They launch a public campaign: petitions, archives, press. Tamsin claims her story openly, including the fire, and the village responds with unexpected grace. Beat: redemption through community.

chapters.title: The Rival Bid
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. A developer counters with money and jobs; a councilor leaks Tamsin's past to discredit her. Beat: external crisis weaponizing internal wound.

chapters.title: Standing in the Paper
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Front-page story: 'Keeper's Granddaughter Owns Her Past.' Instead of shame, villagers share their own secrets at the bookshop. Beat: belonging earned.

chapters.title: Departure Eve
chapters.summary: Dual POV. September 30th. Airport or hearing? Callum stays illegally one extra day; they prepare her testimony together through the night. Beat: love against duty, literally.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Climax: she testifies — about the fire, the letters, the light. Callum, facing arrest for overstaying, stands as her witness. The committee deliberates. Beat: everything risked.

chapters.title: The Lamp Relit
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Heritage status granted; the developer withdraws; immigration grants Callum a heritage-skills visa as the tower's keeper. They climb the gallery and light the lamp together. Beat: triumph and union.

chapters.title: Letters, Signed
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Epilogue-ish: they publish the twelve letters alongside her novel; her grandfather's final entry read aloud at the relighting ceremony. Beat: memory honored, circle closed.

chapters.title: The Sweet Summer
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing chapter. One year later: the light turns nightly, the bookshop window holds her novel, two mugs on the keeper's cottage table. Tamsin writes the last line of a new book. Beat: peace that isn't hiding — belonging chosen daily.
